blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre retórica e oratória a partir de uma resenha, avaliando argumentos e estilo com critérios precisos.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Review: The Art of the Pause by Helen Marsh
paras: Helen Marsh’s new study of public speaking is **at once** a manual and an essay. Its central claim, that **silence persuades more than volume**, is **argued with conviction** and **illustrated with** speeches from three centuries. Marsh is **at her best** when she **dissects** a single paragraph, **showing** where a speaker breathes and why.

The book is **not without flaws**. Its middle chapters **labour the point**, and a few examples feel **cherry-picked**. Even so, it **rewards** a patient reader. **Whether or not** you agree with her, you will **never hear** a speech in quite the same way.

items.q: The book is only a manual.
The reviewer finds the middle chapters repetitive.
The reviewer recommends the book to impatient readers.

items.why: labour the point = insistir além do necessário.

blocks.body: Resenhas equilibradas usam **litote** (*not without flaws*), **concessão** (*even so*) e **verbos de avaliação** (*dissects, rewards, labours*).
*Not without flaws* = “tem defeitos” (tom suave). Não confunda com *flawless* (sem defeitos).

items.s: Marsh is ___ her best when she dissects a paragraph. (at)
___ so, it rewards a patient reader. (even)
Whether ___ not you agree, it is stimulating. (or)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Would you recommend the Marsh book
items.pt: Você recomendaria o livro de Marsh?

body: **At once… and…** — Ao mesmo tempo… e…
**Not without flaws.** — Não sem defeitos.
**Labour the point.** — Insistir demais.
**Read like a novel.** — Ler como um romance.
**Hit the mark.** — Acertar o alvo.
**Fall flat.** — Não funcionar.
**A tour de force.** — Uma proeza.
**Worth its weight in gold.** — Vale ouro.
**Sit up and take notice.** — Prestar atenção.
**Leave a lasting impression.** — Deixar marca duradoura.
**Would you recommend the Marsh book?** — Você recomendaria o livro de Marsh?
**Is the argument convincing?** — O argumento convence?
**Whether or not you agree, it’s stimulating.** — Concorde ou não, é estimulante.

prompts.q: Praise a book with at her best.
prompts.model: The author is at her best when she explains.
The plot is not without holes.
The pace is slow; even so, it rewards patience.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence review of a book, talk or documentary about public speaking, balancing praise and criticism.
blocks.model: This documentary on great speeches is at once moving and instructive. It is at its best when it lets the original recordings play uninterrupted. The narration, however, labours the point and sometimes states the obvious. Not every example is well chosen. Even so, it rewards close attention. I would recommend it to anyone who speaks in public.
